note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Width-dependent heterogeneity bound in FedAvg, linearization, centralized equivalence, and experiments

nodes.name: Non-IID data hampers FL
nodes.description: Client data in federated learning are non-IID, causing divergent local optimizations that degrade global model convergence and generalization.

nodes.name: Prior analyses need restrictive assumptions
nodes.description: Prior convergence analyses of FedAvg under non-IID data rely on convexity, bounded gradient dissimilarity or bounded gradients, which are hard to satisfy in practice.

nodes.name: Model divergence bounded by width
nodes.description: For multi-layer overparameterized networks trained with FedAvg and GD, the model divergence caused by data heterogeneity is bounded and decays as O(n^{-1/2}) in the network width n, without convexity or gradient-boundedness assumptions (Theorem 1).

nodes.name: Heterogeneity slows convergence, vanishes at infinite width
nodes.description: The heterogeneity term zeta = O(n^{-1/2}) slows the convergence rate and leaves nonzero convergence error, but as n approaches infinity zeta tends to 0 and the impact of data heterogeneity vanishes (Remark 2).

nodes.name: Global and local models linearize
nodes.description: As width goes to infinity, both global and local FedAvg models stay within O(n^{-1/2}) of their first-order Taylor linearizations and have constant global and local NTKs (Theorem 2).

nodes.name: Closed-form linear FedAvg dynamics
nodes.description: In the infinite-width limit with small learning rate, the linear global model has closed-form parameters and outputs through training (Theorem 3).

nodes.name: Infinite-width FedAvg equals centralized GD
nodes.description: Infinite-width FedAvg and centralized GD yield identical model parameters and outputs under matched iterations, hence the same generalization performance.

nodes.name: Test accuracy gap shrinks with width
nodes.description: On non-IID versus IID data, the test accuracy drop shrinks as width grows: FNN1/2/4/16 drop 17.4%/9.5%/6.3%/2.0%, CNN1/2/8/32 drop 44.9%/26.7%/5.1%/2.4%, ResNet1/2/4/16 drop 44.6%/29.1%/18.7%/14.8%.

nodes.name: Wide nets nearly equal on IID and non-IID
nodes.description: With learning rate eta0/n, the convergence rate and final accuracy of FNN32 and CNN32 are nearly identical for IID and non-IID data, while FNN1 and CNN1 show a noticeable gap.

nodes.name: NTK and parameters near-constant when wide
nodes.description: Increasing width diminishes variations in global and local NTKs and model parameters; sufficiently wide networks show nearly constant NTKs and parameters (lazy training).

nodes.name: Linear approximation tighter for wide nets
nodes.description: The outputs of the global and local models stay nearly identical to their linear models for FNN512 but visibly differ for FNN16.

nodes.name: FedAvg matches centralized learning empirically
nodes.description: Experiments comparing overparameterized FedAvg with centralized learning show the same generalization behaviour, confirming Theorem 3.

isolated_nodes.name: Communication-efficient FL idea
isolated_nodes.description: Because model outputs depend linearly on parameters, clients might transmit only model outputs instead of full parameters, potentially reducing communication; this is proposed for future work.

isolated_nodes.name: First quantitative width-heterogeneity link
isolated_nodes.description: This is claimed to be the first work quantitatively linking network width to the impact of data heterogeneity on FL training and generalization.

isolated_nodes.name: Experimental setup
isolated_nodes.description: Experiments use MNIST and CIFAR-10 with Dirichlet non-IID partition over M=10 clients, FNN/CNN/ResNet architectures with varied width, different losses and optimizers.

structural_reasoning: Problem and assumptions lead to the width-dependent bound, then linearization and closed-form dynamics yield centralized equivalence; experiments each validate a corresponding theoretical statement.
